title: Inference telemetry minimization and proof-of-deletion annex (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This annex defines contractual commitments and practical procedures for telemetry minimization and provable deletion of inference-related telemetry generated by Redwood Inference when acting as processor for Customer workloads. It is intended to be attached to DPAs, Managed Service Agreements, or Private Deployment terms where Customer requires reduced telemetry footprint and audit evidence for deletion of sensitive inference-derived traces.

Principles:
- Minimize: collect only telemetry strictly necessary to deliver the service, maintain safety, and meet SLA diagnostics.
- Ephemeral by default: inference-specific context (prefixes, KV caches, request payloads) is treated as ephemeral unless Customer explicitly elects retention.
- Provable deletion: Redwood will provide verifiable evidence that retained telemetry was purged according to agreed schedules and scope.
- Exceptions: retention may be required for security investigations, legal holds, or troubleshooting; such exceptions, scope and retention windows are explicitly documented and audited.

Definitions (for contract reference):
- Inference telemetry: logs, traces, sampled inputs/outputs, input hashes, intermediate KV cache metadata, and runtime diagnostics produced during model inference. excludes system health telemetry (CPU/GPU metrics aggregated at host level) unless it contains identifiable request payloads.
- Ephemeral retention window: default 0–72 hours depending on customer tier and troubleshooting flags.
- Proof-of-deletion artifact: tamper-evident record (signed manifest) that lists deleted artifacts, deletion timestamps, method used, and cryptographic checksum of deletion markers.

Commitments (Operational):
1) Collection minimization:
   - Default collection only: request id, timestamp, model id/version, latencies, error codes, route identifiers. No request payloads or full response bodies are stored by default.
   - Conditional sampling: payload or partial-output sampling is opt-in per-customer, controlled via the Console. Sampling rates and filters must be declared and are subject to audit.

2) Retention windows and retention classes:
   - Class A (Ephemeral): raw request and response payloads — default retention 0–72h.
   - Class B (Short-term diagnostics): aggregated traces and top-level token counts — retention 30 days by default.
   - Class C (Long-term metrics): anonymized usage and billing aggregates — retention 24 months.
   - Customer may contractually request narrower windows; Redwood will conform where technically possible and reasonably practicable.

3) Proof-of-deletion process:
   - Deletion trigger: scheduled expiration, customer-initiated deletion request, or deletion as part of onboarding/offboarding.
   - Deletion action: data is removed from hot caches, then purged from object stores and backups per the deletion schedule. For encrypted-at-rest objects, encryption key rotation/zeroization is used to render data unrecoverable where applicable.
   - Evidence package: after deletion, Redwood will produce a signed manifest that contains:
       * scope id (customer id, environment, data-class),
       * list of deleted object identifiers or deletion query fingerprints,
       * deletion timestamps (UTC),
       * deletion method code (e.g., HOT_CACHE_FLUSH, OBJECT_STORE_ERASE, KEY_ZEROIZE),
       * cryptographic digest of the manifest (SHA-256) and Redwood signature (PGP or similar).
   - Delivery: manifest delivered to Customer Console and via email API to designated DPO contact.

4) Verification and third-party attestations:
   - Redwood will retain internal audit logs (access/evidence of deletion operations) for 90 days to support verification requests.
   - Annual attestation: for customers on Enterprise/Private plans, Redwood will include proof-of-deletion sampling in the annual SOC/ISO attestation scope or provide a scoped third-party deletion verification report.
   - On-demand verification: Customer may request up to two deletion verifications per contract year. Redwood will run a scoped verification (see Verification steps below) and provide a signed verification report within 30 business days. Additional requests may be charged.

5) Exceptions and legal holds:
   - If Redwood receives a lawful request (subpoena, government order) requiring preservation of telemetry, Redwood will notify Customer in accordance with the Agreement (unless prohibited) and preserve only the minimal subset as required. Such preserved data will be clearly marked and excluded from standard deletion schedules until the hold is lifted.

Technical verification steps (scoped procedure to be used for internal runbooks and external verification requests):
- Step V1: Scope identification — collect Customer environment identifiers, data classes, timeframe.
- Step V2: Reproduce deletion query — build the exact deletion queries used and disclose hashes/fingerprints to Customer verifier.
- Step V3: Confirm storage drains — show object store manifests pre- and post-deletion (redacted identifiers as needed), and provide storage-level tombstone markers.
- Step V4: Key evidence check — for encryption-backed deletion, provide key version rotation logs showing zeroization event IDs and KMS audit links.
- Step V5: Immutable logs & signature verification — provide signed manifest and chain-of-custody audit events for the deletion operation.
- Step V6: Randomized sampling — Redwood will allow Customer (or Customer-approved auditor) to select a randomized sample of deleted object fingerprints and Redwood will provide original delete markers and corresponding proof records.

Acceptance criteria for deletion verification:
- Artifacts in the evidence package are correctly signed and timestamps are consistent with deletion request.
- For sampled items, object identifiers or fingerprints are present in pre-deletion and in deletion manifests.
- Key zeroization events correlate to deletion windows where applicable.
- No operational errors were recorded in the deletion job logs for the scoped timeframe.

Operational controls and configuration options offered to Customers:
- Console toggles for payload-sampling (off by default), with UI showing current sampling rate and live counters.
- Per-route retention overrides (e.g., support route 'debug' retains 7 days while normal routes remain ephemeral).
- Automated redaction: Customer may supply a regex or named field list for auto-redaction of request payloads before any storage. Redwood validates regex performance impact prior to activation.

Audit rights and escalation:
- Redwood grants Customers the right to request deletion verification as described. For deep-dive audits, Redwood reserves the right to require a mutual NDA and scope agreement before granting direct access to internal logs or to coordinate with a mutually agreed third-party auditor.
- Escalation timeline: Redwood will acknowledge verification requests within 3 business days and provide preliminary evidence or a mitigation plan within 10 business days.

Sample contract language (to be inserted into a DPA or Annex):
"Redwood shall collect and retain inference telemetry only to the extent necessary to provide the Services. Unless Customer expressly configures retention options in writing, Redwood shall treat all request/response payloads as Ephemeral (Class A) and shall delete such data within seventy-two (72) hours. Following deletion Redwood shall provide Customer with a signed proof-of-deletion manifest including deletion scope, timestamps, deletion method, and cryptographic signature. Customer may request up to two (2) deletion verifications per 12-month period. Requests for additional verifications will be subject to a reasonable fee and scheduling. Redwood may preserve data subject to lawful process, in which case Redwood shall notify Customer unless prohibited by law."

Operational notes for engineering (non-contractual):
- Implement per-customer retention configs as metadata on S3 prefixes; scheduled lifecycle jobs emit deletion manifests to a per-customer secure artifact bucket with KMS encryption.
- Backups: snapshot lifecycle must be annotated with retention-class; snapshots that include ephemeral telemetry must be eligible for expedited purge pathways when deletion is requested.
- Logging: maintain immutable access logs for deletion jobs for 90 days to support forensics.

Open questions & risks (internal):
- Backup purging guarantees across clouds — some object-store provider retention mechanics (e.g., cross-region replication) delay physical deletion. Need explicit contractual language about reasonable efforts and timeline expectations.
- Cost model for on-demand verifications and large-volume deletion proofs — require pricing appendix.
- Performance impact of aggressive redaction/sampling in high-throughput serving runtime — engineering to provide benchmarks (see jira:SEC-3421).

Next steps (action items):
- Legal: convert annex into DPA clause with cleanly scoped breach and liability lines — assignee: Maya (due 2024-12-10).
- Eng: produce a runbook prototype and implementation spike for signed manifests — assignee: Samir (due 2025-01-15).
- Product: add Console UI mock for sampling toggles and retention display — assignee: Jordan (due 2024-12-20).

Notes to reviewers:
This document is intentionally prescriptive on operational evidence formats to make audits practical — feedback requested on the manifest schema, signature method, and the number of allowed on-demand verifications. Also confirm that the retention default windows align with existing Hosted and Dedicated product commitments.
